clue.text: LA gang member this evening reported threat to hero

indicators.note: reported means the words are as heard, spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a Crip is a member of the Crips, a Los Angeles street gang; this evening is tonight

explanation.surface: A news item about a Los Angeles gangster said to be menacing some hero tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIP TONIGHT said aloud matches the answer, spelt as in the Superman stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Kryptonite is the green mineral that robs Superman of his powers, the classic menace to a comic-book hero.

clue.text: Bananas stay in sack in stateside location

indicators.note: Bananas means crazy, so the letters of the following words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone told to lie in bed in some American place.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas City is a major US city straddling Missouri and Kansas, so a place in the States.

clue.text: Met leader for job as American rail coordinator

parts.note: the Met, London's Metropolitan Police, is based at New Scotland Yard, known as the Yard
a master is a leader or head

explanation.surface: A London police chief taking a job running American railways.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pictures a head of Scotland Yard, as if the Met's chief were called its master.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardmaster supervises a railway yard, directing the shunting and making-up of trains, a US job title.

clue.text: Compassion that made Pansy barmy over years

indicators.note: over in this down clue means the scrambled words sit above the abbreviation for years
barmy means crazy, so the fodder letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Sympathy that sent someone called Pansy mad over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea and sympathy is the idiom for kindly comfort offered to someone in distress.

clue.text: Homes in northeast are mostly small

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A claim that houses in the northeast are mainly small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homes' looks like houses; with 'in' it is the verb phrase 'homes in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that homes in is approaching its target, drawing closer to it.

clue.text: Sausage variety, one almost identical to another, needed by Thursday

parts.note: a ringer, as in a dead ringer, is a lookalike

explanation.surface: A sausage type, nearly the same as another, wanted by Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuringer is a smoked or semi-dry German style of sausage from Thuringia.

clue.text: Suggestive banter from Greek character in street

indicators.note: in places the Greek letter within the abbreviation for street

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Cheeky innuendo heard from a Greek figure out in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent or risqué talk, the kind of banter that leans toward the obscene.

clue.text: Current in which British sailors lost way

indicators.note: lost means the sailors are taken out of the word for current

parts.note: current means present-day, modern
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's sailors

explanation.surface: A sea current in which a British crew lost its bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests a flow of water for the sailors; here it means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a manner or method of doing something, as in mode of transport.

clue.text: Ultimately unpleasant eccentric in Sweeney?

indicators.note: Ultimately means the last letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: eccentric means odd

explanation.surface: A nasty oddball, like the murderous barber of Fleet Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweeney' might suggest the TV police show; here it is Sweeney Todd, the demon barber of Fleet Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeney Todd is the fictional barber, so the surname is the word found alongside Sweeney in his name.

clue.text: Drill to assist one attempting to strike gold?

definitions.text: Drill to assist one attempting to strike gold?

parts.words: Drill to assist one attempting to strike gold?
parts.note: suggests mining for gold, but the gold is the centre of an archery target

explanation.walkthrough: Striking gold sounds like prospecting with a drill; in archery the bullseye is gold, and a drill is a training exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting practice at a marked board is repeated training aimed at hitting its centre, the gold.

clue.text: Spiritual liberation Irish see, taken in by simpleton

indicators.note: taken in by means the first pieces are enclosed by the word for simpleton

parts.note: a nana is a fool, a silly person
V is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: An Irish bishop's see is fooled by a simpleton, framed as a quest for enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a diocese or a verb of looking; here it is V, from the Latin vide. A nana is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism the state of release from the cycle of rebirth and suffering is called by this word.

clue.text: One French assistant died alone

parts.note: un is French for one
an aide is an assistant
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A lonely French helper who passed away by himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unaided means doing it without help, on one's own, by oneself.

clue.text: Delivering reprimand, bashed him in gonads

indicators.note: bashed means the letters of the following words are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone telling a man off by striking him below the belt.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to scold or rebuke someone firmly, so the participle means giving a telling-off.

clue.text: I put on stone? Some would some call me bloated!

definitions.text: Some would some call me bloated

indicators.note: put on means, in this down clue, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the letter I written upper-case is a capital I
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A self-mocking fat person asks if they've gained a stone, admitting some call them bloated.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'some' is a slip in the clue as set. 'Bloated capitalist' is a stock insult, so the answer speaks for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloated capitalist is a stock leftist jibe at the rich, so this is who some would call bloated.

clue.text: Barely crawls, but dances round pub yard?

indicators.note: round means the word for dances goes around the other pieces

parts.note: skips means hops or dances
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone barely crawling yet dancing round a pub's yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' looks like 'hardly'; here it means naked, and crawls are swimming strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny-dipping is swimming naked, so going for crawls in the bare.

clue.text: Goes for son in bed with temptress at last

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for son inside the small bed

parts.note: a cot is a child's bed

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of temptress

explanation.surface: A son seduced and taken to bed by a temptress in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes for' looks like 'attacks' or 'chooses', but it is the price sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An item that costs ten pounds sells for that price; 'goes for' is the same idiom of sale value.

clue.text: Say Neil's defensive position?

indicators.note: Say indicates that the phrase is to be spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Neil is LIEN written back, so the name prompts the phrase 'write back'

explanation.surface: Asks what defensive role a man named Neil plays, as if in a football team.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Neil is the word LIEN spelt backwards, i.e. LIEN 'written back'; spoken, 'write back' sounds like the football position.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the right back is a defender stationed on the right side of the team's back line.

clue.text: Were Marx and Engels such huge stars?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: communist titans, red as in left-wing, giants as in great thinkers
second meaning: large, cool stars late in their life

explanation.walkthrough: Marx and Engels were towering figures of communism, so 'red' giants.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers call large, cool, expanded stars near the end of their lives red giants.

clue.text: Seafood so cooked, I had men joining the Marines

parts.note: the is taken as written
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines
I had contracts to I'd
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A cook's boast about a seafood dish, with soldiers enlisting in the Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' here means other ranks, ordinary soldiers, not officers; 'joining' lets the later pieces come first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobster Thermidor is a dish of lobster meat cooked in a creamy sauce and served in the shell.

clue.text: Good to be in control for time as ruler

indicators.note: to be in means the abbreviation for good is placed inside the word for control

parts.note: to rein is to control or restrain, as a horse

explanation.surface: A homily that being good is the way to stay in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period during which they hold the throne.

clue.text: Heartless character is given to Conservative Blue Elite

indicators.note: Heartless means the middle letter of the word for character is removed

parts.note: air is character or bearing, as in an air of confidence
given to means to, as in 'is given to' a person
blue means risqué, as does racy

explanation.surface: A political description of a character joining the Tories as a blue-blooded elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like the Tory colour beside 'Conservative'; here it means smutty, RACY. AIR loses its centre I to give AR.
explanation.definitionFit: The aristocracy is the hereditary nobility, a privileged upper class standing at society's top.

clue.text: Section in Beckett: it lends play's name

indicators.note: Section in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A literary note about a passage of Beckett lending a play its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a work such as a play.

clue.text: Old festival crowd put up in Floridian mansion

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
to ram is to cram or crowd in

explanation.surface: An old festival crowd hosted at a grand Florida house.
explanation.definitionFit: Mar-a-Lago is Donald Trump's Palm Beach estate and club in Florida.

clue.text: See 21
Silver brought to a king by Chinese leader

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Han are the majority ethnic group of China

explanation.surface: A silver gift taken to a king by a Chinese ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese leader' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aga Khan is the hereditary spiritual head of the Nizari Ismaili Muslims, a religious figurehead.

clue.text: City built is fantastic one displacing upper-class

indicators.note: fantastic signals that the letters are rearranged into a wild new form
displacing means one letter ousts another, taking its place in the fodder

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Praise of a fantastically built city where a single person ousts the posh set.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the U of BUILT IS for I, giving BIILTIS, then rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia, in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Alpha male causing scrap

parts.note: Alpha is A in the phonetic alphabet
a tom is a male animal, especially a cat

explanation.surface: An alpha male picking a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight, fitting the alpha male; it is a tiny fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest particle, so the word means a tiny bit, as in 'not an atom of truth'.

clue.text: Female guides American canine back to welcome ambassador

indicators.note: to welcome means the outer letters take in the ambassador's title
back means the dog's name is read in reverse

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Women showing visitors round, with an American dog turning back to greet an envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Usherettes are women who show people to their seats in a cinema or theatre.
